steps.title: Base & PWM Speed Control
steps.description: Place the PWM speed controller PCB inside the weighted desktop base and press the knurled aluminum speed knob onto the vertical potentiometer shaft.

steps.title: Tilt Yoke & Motor Pod
steps.description: Mount the U-shaped tilt yoke to the base pedestal, position the vented motor housing at its 12-degree upward tilt, and secure both side trunnions with the locking thumb knobs.

steps.title: Motor, Axle & Sourced 608 Bearing
steps.description: Install the brushless DC motor inside the housing, slide the 8 mm stainless drive axle through the motor, and press the sourced 608 ball bearing (8 mm bore, 22 mm OD) into the front nose boss.

steps.title: Circular Grille & Exposed Three-Blade Rotor
steps.description: Fasten the open-front circular safety grille around the motor pod and press the high-visibility three-blade rotor hub onto the protruding 8 mm axle in front of the 608 bearing.

relationships.description: Weighted base encloses the PWM motor speed controller PCB.
Knurled aluminum speed knob couples to the potentiometer shaft on the control PCB.
PWM controller delivers variable-duty DC power through the yoke cable to the brushless motor.
U-shaped tilt yoke bolts rigidly to the top pedestal of the weighted base.
Tilt yoke cradles the motor housing side trunnions at a 12-degree upward angle.
Threaded thumb knobs clamp the yoke arms against the motor housing trunnions to lock the tilt angle.
Vented rear motor pod houses the brushless DC stator and rotor.
Front 22 mm nose pocket of the motor housing seats the outer race of the sourced 608 ball bearing.
Brushless DC motor drives the 8 mm stainless steel fan axle.
Sourced 608 bearing supports the 8 mm fan axle with low-friction rolling contact.
Front end of the 8 mm axle press-fits into the exposed three-blade rotor hub.
Circular safety grille mounts to the motor housing perimeter and pivot bosses.

rounds.summary: The desktop fan assembly preserves all original component shapes and the sourced 608 ball bearing, but the U-Shaped Tilt Yoke is currently lowered to Y = 48 mm, causing solid collisions across the -45 to +45 degree tilt sweep. Specifically, the U-Shaped Tilt Yoke intersects the PWM Speed Controller PCB across all sampled angles, and the Circular Rear & Perimeter Safety Grille collides with both the Knurled Speed Knob and the Weighted Base Stand. Raising the U-Shaped Tilt Yoke to [0, 78, 0] mm stays within the declared position limits, keeps the stand at least 10 mm shorter than the original reference height, and restores clearance for the full tilt range. Physical operation, structural strength, and electrical performance remain unverified.

observations.detail: At the lowered U-Shaped Tilt Yoke height of Y = 48 mm, the stand is shorter than the original reference, but the U-Shaped Tilt Yoke intersects the PWM Speed Controller PCB and the Circular Rear & Perimeter Safety Grille collides with the Knurled Speed Knob and Weighted Base Stand.

Although the revolute joint sweeps from -45 to +45 degrees relative to the -12 degree resting angle of the Tilted Motor Pod & Bearing Boss, the motion check fails across all 19 sampled poses due to interference at the lowered stand height.

Sampled motion clearance fails with 0 mm clearance between the PWM Speed Controller PCB and U-Shaped Tilt Yoke from -45 to +45 degrees, between the Knurled Speed Knob and Circular Rear & Perimeter Safety Grille from -20 to +20 degrees, and between the Weighted Base Stand and Circular Rear & Perimeter Safety Grille from 0 to +45 degrees.
The U-Shaped Tilt Yoke is currently positioned at [0, 48, 0] mm and can be raised vertically within the declared [0, 48, 0] mm to [0, 78, 0] mm bounds.
All custom component solids and envelope dimensions match their original baseline shapes across the assembled and exploded views.
The 608 Axle Ball Bearing retains its sourced catalog geometry (22 x 7 x 22 mm) seated in the front boss of the Tilted Motor Pod & Bearing Boss.
